title: The Unix Wars: USL v. BSDi and the Fight Over Open-Source Licensing (1992-94)
explainer: When Berkeley Software Design (BSDi) began selling a Unix-like system built from UC Berkeley's freely redistributable BSD code, AT&T's Unix System Laboratories sued in 1992, claiming the code still carried AT&T trade secrets and copyrights. The case was settled in 1994 after the judge found USL's copyright claims shaky, clearing a path for BSD-derived systems to be freely distributed — a reminder that the licensing terms under which you're allowed to fork, copy, and redistribute a real systems codebase were often fought out in exactly this kind of courtroom dispute over code provenance.
